confirmed_facts.fact: RidgeCode already uses Viewport::Inline and Terminal::insert_before through insert_bounded_commit_lines; before this slice, each committed block independently invoked the bounded insertion helper during one flush.
confirmed_facts.evidence: crates/agent/src/tui/app.rs flush_commits, insert_commit, activity_commit_lines, colored_commit_lines, insert_bounded_commit_lines; crates/agent/src/tui/tests.rs static_scrollback_preserves_order_and_sanitizes_controls.

contradictions.claim: A new hardware scroll/DECSTBM module is required.
contradictions.local_evidence: The existing inline viewport already owns native scrollback insertion. The compatible local gap is only repeated per-block insertion boundaries, not a missing hardware primitive.

unverified_hypotheses.hypothesis: Coalescing the existing pure committed-line projections before the bounded insert_before batches reduces redundant scroll/cursor boundary work without changing native scrollback order.
support: flush_commits previously called the insertion helper once per CommitBlock.
against: The current 8-row bound still creates multiple insert_before calls for very large output, and no fixed latency improvement is claimed.
unverified_hypotheses.experiment: Aggregate mixed Answer/Reasoning/Activity/Tool projections in one flush, retain the existing 8-row insertion bound, and verify order, sanitization, CJK/Markdown wrapping, resize, HOLD/FOLLOW, takeover, and ConPTY.

candidates.core: Coalesce existing presentation-only commit lines per flush, then pass the combined wrapped vector once to the existing bounded native-scrollback inserter.
constraints: retain Viewport::Inline, Terminal::insert_before, 8-row bound, block order, blank separators, folding, sanitization, and all key/execution semantics
no DECSTBM module, dependency, second renderer, cache, or action channel
risks: mixed blocks must preserve exact order and width wrapping; very large output must remain chunked by the existing bound
validation: mixed static order/sanitization and PARTIAL Answer regressions

recommendation: Reject the duplicate hardware-scroll layer. Accept only the local coalescing boundary, with no latency or O(1) claim until measured.

next_step.value: Project all CommitBlocks to wrapped Lines first, then invoke the existing bounded insert_before path once per flush.

stop_conditions: Do not add DECSTBM/scrolling-region code, a second renderer/cache/parser, or a fixed performance threshold.
Do not change Answer/Reasoning/Tool/Activity text, order, folding, queue, HOLD/FOLLOW, takeover, Tab/Enter, or Ctrl-C semantics.
Do not query old Deep Research status or create a Note/source.
If any mixed-block order, wrapping, or ConPTY regression appears, revert the coalescing boundary.
